newsitem.title: UK: London gold market puzzles over central bank sales.
newsitem.headline: London gold market puzzles over central bank sales.

text.p: Gold prices held steady on Monday afternoon while the bullion market puzzled over fresh news about central bank gold reserve sales.

Values had edged up early in the day after the Dutch Central Bank said it had sold 300 tonnes of gold from its reserves, apparently on a sense of relief at getting some facts after months of rumour about central bank selling of bullion. But the market registered no price reaction to a later statement by Bundesbank president Hans Teitmayer, that the Group of 10 central banks saw no need to sell gold for the time being to boost national revenues.
Bullion was fixed unchanged at $359.60 in the afternoon.

"People were a little unsure as to whether (the Dutch sales) were bullish or bearish," a senior bullion trader said."Short term it may be constructive because now we can see why the market's come off $30. It's out of the way now," he said.
Rumours of a sale from a central bank of around 10 million ounces (300 tonnes) had been current in the market for weeks and were a key factor behind gold's loss of value late last year.
The G10 news that there was no intention to sell gold "for the time being" generated more confusion, dealers said.
"People aren't reacting to it because they don't understand what it really means," one trader said.
"It's just the G10 waffling," another noted.
The eleven members of the so-called G10 are Belgium, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Sweden, the United States and Switzerland.
The Dutch news came after the gold price had bounced off 3-1/4 year lows struck last week after gold's downtrend began to accelerate from the beginning of the year.
"The (Dutch) news is probably bullish short term and bearish long term," said bullion analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland. "People are probably buying the volatility."

Longer term the sale raised the spectre about other central banks selling some of their gold reserves, particularly those keen to bring their budget deficits in line with European Monetary Union requirements, analysts said.

The Dutch bank said the bullion sales represented more than 20 percent of its total holdings. This was less than 400 tonnes or some 25 percent of its then gold reserves that a spokesman said it disposed of in an earlier November-December 1992 sale.
The other precious metals were easier. Silver eased six cents to $4.70/$4.72, platinum was down $1.80 at $362.70/$363.70 and pallaidum was down $0.50 at $122.00/$123.00.
